RSA by RDM Correlation¶

API Details¶

a module for calculating the Similarity (Spearman Correlation Cosfficient) between model RDMs and neural RDMs

neurora.corr_cal_by_rdm.fmrirdms_corr(model_rdms, fmri_rdms, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky')¶

Calculate Spearman correlations between multiple model RDMs and fMRI searchlight RDMs.

Parameters:

  • model_rdms (array_like, shape [n_models, n_cons, n_cons]) –

    Model RDMs.

    Each model RDM can be a behavioral RDM, a hypothesis-based coding model RDM, or a computational model RDM.

  • fmri_rdms (array_like, shape [n_x, n_y, n_z, n_cons, n_cons]) –

    fMRI searchlight RDMs.

    n_x, n_y, and n_z represent the number of searchlight units along the x, y, and z axes.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to use joblib-based parallel computation across fMRI searchlight RDMs.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) –

    Number of workers used when parallel=True.

    If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"threading", "loky"}, default="loky") –

    Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

    Use “threading” for shared-memory parallelism and lower memory overhead. Use “loky” for process-based parallelism when CPU-bound Python code is the main bottleneck.

Returns:

corrs – Spearman correlation results between each fMRI searchlight RDM and each model RDM.

The last dimension contains:

  • corrs[…, 0] : Spearman r

  • corrs[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_x, n_y, n_z, n_models, 2]

neurora.corr_cal_by_rdm.fmrirdms_corr_perm(model_rdms, fmri_rdms, n_permutation=1000, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky', random_state=None)¶

Calculate permutation-based Spearman correlations between model RDMs and fMRI searchlight RDMs.

The permutation is performed by shuffling the condition labels of each fMRI searchlight RDM.

Parameters:

  • model_rdms (array_like, shape [n_models, n_cons, n_cons]) – Model RDMs.

  • fmri_rdms (array_like, shape [n_x, n_y, n_z, n_cons, n_cons]) – fMRI searchlight RDMs.

  • n_permutation (int, default=1000) – Number of condition-label permutations.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across fMRI searchlight units.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True.

  • backend ({"threading", "loky"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

  • random_state (int or None, default=None) – Random seed.

Returns:

perm_corrs – Permutation Spearman correlation results.

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_x, n_y, n_z, n_permutation, n_models, 2]

neurora.corr_cal_by_rdm.fmrirdms_partialcorr(model_rdms, fmri_rdms, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky')¶

Calculate Spearman partial correlations between multiple model RDMs and fMRI searchlight RDMs.

For each model RDM, the partial correlation is computed between the fMRI searchlight RDM and the current model RDM while controlling for all other model RDMs.

Parameters:

  • model_rdms (array_like, shape [n_models, n_cons, n_cons]) –

    Model RDMs.

    Each model RDM can be a behavioral RDM, a hypothesis-based coding model RDM, or a computational model RDM.

  • fmri_rdms (array_like, shape [n_x, n_y, n_z, n_cons, n_cons]) –

    fMRI searchlight RDMs.

    n_x, n_y, and n_z represent the number of searchlight units along the x, y, and z axes.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) –

    Whether to use joblib-based parallel computation across fMRI searchlight RDMs.

    Parallelization is performed across searchlight units.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) –

    Number of workers used when parallel=True.

    If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"threading", "loky"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

Returns:

corrs – Spearman partial correlation results between each fMRI searchlight RDM and each model RDM while controlling for the other model RDMs.

The last dimension contains:

  • corrs[…, 0] : Spearman partial correlation coefficient

  • corrs[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_x, n_y, n_z, n_models, 2]

neurora.corr_cal_by_rdm.rdms_corr(model_rdms, eeg_rdms, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky')¶

Calculate Spearman correlations between multiple model RDMs and EEG-like RDMs.

Parameters:

  • model_rdms (array_like, shape [n_models, n_cons, n_cons]) –

    Model RDMs.

    Each model RDM can be a behavioral RDM, a hypothesis-based coding model RDM, or a computational model RDM.

  • eeg_rdms (array_like) –

    EEG/MEG/fNIRS/ECoG/sEEG/electrophysiological RDMs.

    Supported shapes are:

    • [n_cons, n_cons]

    • [n1, n_cons, n_cons]

    • [n1, n2, n_cons, n_cons]

    • [n1, n2, n3, n_cons, n_cons]

    The leading dimensions can represent time windows, channels, subjects, or other analysis dimensions.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to use joblib-based parallel computation across EEG-like RDMs.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) –

    Number of workers used when parallel=True.

    If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"threading", "loky"}, default="loky") –

    Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

    Use “threading” for shared-memory parallelism and lower memory overhead. Use “loky” for process-based parallelism when CPU-bound Python code is the main bottleneck.

Returns:

corrs – Spearman correlation results between each EEG-like RDM and each model RDM.

If eeg_rdms has shape [n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n_models, 2]

If eeg_rdms has shape [n1, n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n1, n_models, 2]

If eeg_rdms has shape [n1, n2, n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n1, n2, n_models, 2]

If eeg_rdms has shape [n1, n2, n3, n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n1, n2, n3, n_models, 2]

The last dimension contains:

  • corrs[…, 0] : Spearman r

  • corrs[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray

neurora.corr_cal_by_rdm.rdms_corr_perm(model_rdms, eeg_rdms, n_permutation=1000, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky', random_state=None)¶

Calculate permutation-based Spearman correlations between model RDMs and EEG-like RDMs.

The permutation is performed by shuffling the condition labels of each EEG-like RDM.

Parameters:

  • model_rdms (array_like, shape [n_models, n_cons, n_cons]) – Model RDMs.

  • eeg_rdms (array_like, shape [..., n_cons, n_cons]) – EEG-like RDMs.

  • n_permutation (int, default=1000) – Number of condition-label permutations.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across EEG-like target RDMs.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True.

  • backend ({"threading", "loky"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

  • random_state (int or None, default=None) – Random seed.

Returns:

perm_corrs – Permutation Spearman correlation results.

Return type:

ndarray, shape […, n_permutation, n_models, 2]

neurora.corr_cal_by_rdm.rdms_partialcorr(model_rdms, eeg_rdms, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky')¶

Calculate Spearman partial correlations between multiple model RDMs and EEG-like RDMs.

For each model RDM, the partial correlation is computed between the EEG-like RDM and the current model RDM while controlling for all other model RDMs.

Parameters:

  • model_rdms (array_like, shape [n_models, n_cons, n_cons]) –

    Model RDMs.

    Each model RDM can be a behavioral RDM, a hypothesis-based coding model RDM, or a computational model RDM.

  • eeg_rdms (array_like) –

    EEG/MEG/fNIRS/ECoG/sEEG/electrophysiological RDMs.

    Supported shapes are:

    • [n_cons, n_cons]

    • [n1, n_cons, n_cons]

    • [n1, n2, n_cons, n_cons]

    • [n1, n2, n3, n_cons, n_cons]

    The leading dimensions can represent time windows, channels, subjects, or other analysis dimensions.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) –

    Whether to use joblib-based parallel computation across EEG-like RDMs.

    Parallelization is performed across target RDMs. For typical EEG-like inputs, this means parallelizing across time windows or across the combination of leading dimensions.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) –

    Number of workers used when parallel=True.

    If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"threading", "loky"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

Returns:

corrs – Spearman partial correlation results between each EEG-like RDM and each model RDM while controlling for the other model RDMs.

If eeg_rdms has shape [n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n_models, 2]

If eeg_rdms has shape [n1, n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n1, n_models, 2]

If eeg_rdms has shape [n1, n2, n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n1, n2, n_models, 2]

If eeg_rdms has shape [n1, n2, n3, n_cons, n_cons], corrs has shape:

  • [n1, n2, n3, n_models, 2]

The last dimension contains:

  • corrs[…, 0] : Spearman partial correlation coefficient

  • corrs[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray
